The problem is in the heredoc detection: `<<` immediately starts heredoc mode and any chars until newline are treated as a marker, so `<< >>` errors. part.text:
Fixed in `caddyconfig/caddyfile/lexer.go:139-175`. The lexer treated any `<<` token prefix as a heredoc start and errored when the marker was invalid. The fix (matching upstream caddyserver/caddy#5761, plus the #5769 empty-marker panic guard):

- A space after `<<` (or a `<<`-prefixed token like `<<<EOF`) now ends the token normally, so `between <<  >>` lexes as plain `<<` / `>>` tokens
- Heredoc detection is skipped inside quoted/backtick tokens (so `"<<"` works)
- "too many `<`" is only reported when `<<<` is actually followed by a newline (an attempted heredoc), and a bare `<<` with no marker gets a clear "missing opening heredoc marker" error instead of panicking

All 20 tests in `caddyconfig/caddyfile` pass, including the previously failing lexer cases; `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.
